Information: IRAPUATO, REIMAGINED is an interactive educational website that explores local challenges in Irapuato, Guanajuato, and imagines how the municipality could evolve by 2050. It connects local information, sustainable development goals, hypothetical future scenarios, and practical ways for residents to participate. The project is educational and independent; it is not an official municipal platform.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: What could Irapuato become by 2050 and what decisions today could help shape that future? The website invites users to explore local issues, compare possible futures, and discover actions that individuals, communities, institutions, and government can take.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: Transform information about Irapuato's local challenges into an engaging interactive experience that helps users understand their community, imagine a more sustainable future, and identify realistic ways to contribute. The project combines local research, visual storytelling, and civic/environmental awareness.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: SDG 6 calls for ensuring availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. In the Irapuato context, the website can explore water supply, groundwater dependence, water use, wastewater, water quality, and the importance of conservation. Local figures must retain their publication year and geographic scope.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 6

Information: SDG 11 aims to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable. For Irapuato, relevant themes include urban planning, transport and mobility, public spaces, housing, waste management, environmental quality, heritage, and resilience.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11

Information: SDG 13 calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. Local exploration can include climate adaptation, risk awareness, resilient planning, environmental education, and decisions that reduce vulnerability. The site should not claim local climate projections unless a specific source supports them.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 13

Information: Water, cities, and climate are interconnected. Urban growth affects demand for water and infrastructure; green areas can support environmental quality and resilience; planning decisions can influence exposure to climate risks. The website treats these goals as connected topics rather than isolated problems.
Source: The Global Goals — SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: The Municipal Development Plan Irapuato 2050 is a long-term planning framework for sustainable, resilient, and competitive municipal development. Its vision places residents' quality of life at the center and addresses environmental sustainability, infrastructure, social cohesion, governance, and economic development. The website uses it as a local reference, not as an endorsement or official municipal project.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2050

Topic: Environmental priorities identified by the municipality
Information: Irapuato's municipal environmental program identifies priority themes including biodiversity and natural-resource protection; climate-change mitigation and adaptation; solid-waste management; air-quality improvement; environmental education and awareness; and sustainable water use. These themes can organize the website's local challenge cards.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Protección y Preservación del Ambiente

Information: Municipal planning material describes Irapuato's water supply as relying primarily on groundwater from the Irapuato Valle aquifer, with a smaller portion associated with the Silao-Romita aquifer. The source document also reports that the Irapuato Valle aquifer is subject to water-use restrictions. Treat this as information from the cited municipal document and verify newer updates before publication.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental diagnosis

Information: The municipal government document cites INEGI Census 2020 figures for water-service coverage: 98.61% for the municipality and 94.94% for rural areas. These are historical census-based coverage figures, not a measurement of current water quality, reliability, or water availability. Keep the year visible if displayed as a statistic.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, citing INEGI 2020

Topic: Water extraction data cited in municipal planning
Information: A municipal planning document cites a 2020 concession volume of 58.3 hm³ per year and annual extraction of 37 hm³, from 81 operating wells, with 10 wells in reserve and 11 out of operation. These figures are reported for the year and source context cited in the document; do not label them as current 2026 values.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, citing CONAGUA/JAPAMI planning

Information: How is water used at home, school, in agriculture, and in local industry? Which conservation practices are practical? What information is available about supply, treatment, reuse, and water quality? This card is a set of research questions, not a claim that a particular neighborhood has a specific problem.
Source: Project research prompts; SDG 6; JAPAMI / municipal planning reference

Information: The municipal government planning document identifies Cerro de Arandas and Los Encinos as protected natural areas and reports a combined area of nearly 7,000 hectares. The figure is quoted from that document; check the current official designations and area boundaries before presenting it as an updated inventory.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental section

Information: The municipal planning document reports an approximate 15% loss of forest vegetation area in Irapuato between 2000 and 2018. This is a historical period-specific statistic and should be shown with the years, source, and wording 'reported in the municipal document' rather than as a current rate.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental diagnosis

Topic: Environmental issues described in municipal planning
Information: The municipal program identifies environmental challenges including air pollution, vulnerability to climate change, solid-waste pollution, and loss of biodiversity and natural resources. These can be presented as the municipality's documented priority challenges, not as a ranking or current measurement of severity.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027

Information: A municipal public-information notice explains that burning crop residues, tires, trash, or other materials can release harmful pollutants and affect air quality, health, water, ecosystems, and fire safety. It encourages reporting relevant incidents through municipal channels. The notice gives 072 and 911 as reporting options; users should confirm the appropriate channel and emergency circumstances before use.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Environmental awareness notice, May 24, 2025

Information: The Plan Maestro del Sistema de Parques Irapuato 2050 describes a long-term vision for parks, plazas, and public spaces. It identifies uneven green infrastructure development, maintenance, coverage, and management as planning challenges and proposes a coordinated system of parks. Use the source to discuss planning themes; do not invent park-access measurements.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Maestro del Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: The PMDUOET is a municipal planning instrument guiding land-use decisions, including conservation, development, and urbanization. Its planning framework includes diagnosis, scenarios, sustainable territorial planning, policy instruments, projects, administration, coordination, and evaluation. This helps explain why growth needs planning rather than being presented as inherently negative.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — PMDUOET

Topic: Municipal vision: resilient and sustainable city
Information: The municipal government program describes a resilient city as one that can adapt to climate change and its impacts. It emphasizes planning that protects residents, property, and infrastructure, and promotes clean, safe, functional, inclusive public spaces and sustainable resource management. This is a policy vision, not a guarantee of outcomes.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027

Information: The Municipal Development Plan 2050 highlights strategic projects including transport infrastructure, non-motorized mobility, public transport, parks and green-blue infrastructure, and use of treated water. These are stated planning priorities. The website can explain them and invite users to consider access, safety, and sustainability without claiming that projects are already completed.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2050

Information: IMPLAN's website lists municipal resources such as the risk atlas update, greenhouse-gas inventory, climate-change program, and conservation-area documents. The database points users to these resources for deeper local research; this record does not summarize specific risk levels or emissions quantities.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — plans, studies, and publications

Information: The municipal regulatory agenda describes a local environmental technical standard addressing disposable plastic carry bags, single-use straws, and expanded-polystyrene packaging. The stated rationale includes plastic-related environmental impacts and problems with public infrastructure, including drainage blockages and flooding. Verify the current regulation and its implementation status before describing it as enforceable today.
Source: Irapuato — Sistema Municipal de Mejora Regulatoria, Agenda Regulatoria

Information: IMPLAN describes the Municipal Development Plan 2050 as informed by participation from residents and different sectors of the municipality. This supports the project's emphasis on civic participation and listening to local perspectives, while the website itself remains an independent student project.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — PMD 2050 and Programa de Gobierno

Information: The simulator shows two illustrative futures for Irapuato. They are qualitative scenarios designed to compare different priorities and decisions, based on local planning documents and SDG themes. They are not scientific forecasts, official predictions, or measured outcomes. Any visual score is a website mechanic, not a real municipal statistic.
Source: Project editorial note; IMPLAN Irapuato; The Global Goals

Topic: Scenario A — Irapuato with sustainable decisions
Information: In this hypothetical 2050, municipal planning and community action prioritize sustainable water management, protecting natural areas, improving public and green spaces, managing waste, considering climate risks, and supporting safe and accessible mobility. Progress would require sustained policies, resources, infrastructure, participation, and evaluation. This is a possible future narrative, not a prediction.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on PMD Irapuato 2050, PMDUOET, and SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: Qualitative indicator: water stewardship. The scenario imagines improved conservation, efficient use, treatment and reuse where appropriate, and transparent planning for water resources. Label the card 'priority strengthened' or 'potential improvement'; do not assign a projected percentage without a verified model or source.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on SDG 6 and municipal planning

Topic: Scenario A — Indicator: Green and public spaces
Information: Qualitative indicator: green and public spaces. This scenario imagines a connected, better planned, more accessible, and cared-for network of parks, plazas, and natural areas. The card describes an aspiration and planning priority, not a measured prediction of hectares or access.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on IMPLAN — Sistema de Parques 2050 and SDG 11

Topic: Scenario A — Indicator: Climate and environmental resilience
Information: Qualitative indicator: climate and environmental resilience. The scenario imagines climate risks integrated into planning, environmental education, preparedness, ecosystem protection, and more resilient public infrastructure. It does not claim that hazards will disappear or that damages will be reduced by a specific amount.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on PMD Irapuato 2050, municipal climate planning, and SDG 13

Information: This hypothetical scenario imagines that sustainability priorities receive insufficient attention or inconsistent implementation. Water stress, pressure on natural areas, waste-management challenges, environmental quality, and uneven public-space access may remain concerns. It is a contrast narrative for reflection, not a prediction that these outcomes will occur.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on municipal environmental diagnosis and SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: Qualitative indicator: water pressure. In this scenario, conservation, planning, and resource-management efforts do not keep pace with needs. The card may say 'challenge persists.' It must not invent a future water shortage, percentage, or date.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on SDG 6 and municipal planning

Information: Qualitative indicator: green-space pressure. This narrative imagines that conservation, park maintenance, and equitable access do not improve enough to meet community needs. It is not a projection of future park acreage or a statement about a specific neighborhood.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on IMPLAN — Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: Qualitative indicator: environmental resilience. In this scenario, adaptation planning, preparedness, environmental education, and ecosystem protection remain insufficiently strengthened. The card describes a possible challenge, not a forecast of specific disasters or impacts.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on municipal environmental priorities and SDG 13

Information: Compare both scenarios using the same themes: water stewardship, green and public spaces, and climate/environmental resilience. Scenario A describes priorities that are strengthened; Scenario B describes challenges that persist. Use text labels and qualitative icons rather than fabricated percentages. Add a visible note that both scenarios are illustrative.
Source: Project editorial note; IMPLAN Irapuato; The Global Goals

Information: The interface can use two buttons: 'Future A — Sustainable Decisions' and 'Future B — Challenges Continue.' Selecting a button updates the image, narrative, and three qualitative indicator cards. Users can switch back and forth to compare. This can be implemented with simple Python/Streamlit state; no AI or scientific model is needed.
Source: Project concept based on original 2050 simulator design

Information: Learn how water is used and managed in the community; avoid unnecessary waste; follow reliable local water information; and consider appropriate water-saving practices at home or school. Personal habits are helpful but do not replace infrastructure, planning, or institutional water management.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 6; municipal water-planning sources

Information: Care for shared spaces, avoid damaging vegetation, respect protected areas, and support community efforts that maintain parks and natural areas. Participate only in activities that are organized, permitted, and safe.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11; IMPLAN Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: Choose reusable items when practical, reduce unnecessary packaging, separate waste according to local rules, and learn about municipal collection or recycling options. Do not assume every material is recyclable in every local program.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11 and SDG 13; municipal regulatory agenda

Information: Avoid burning waste or other materials. Learn about local air-quality concerns and use official channels to report environmental incidents when appropriate. Follow official instructions and do not approach fires or hazardous sites.
Source: Government of Irapuato — environmental awareness notice, May 24, 2025

Information: For trips where it is practical, safe, accessible, and suitable, consider walking, cycling, public transport, or sharing a ride. The website should recognize that choices depend on distance, infrastructure, weather, disability/access needs, and safety; it should not pressure users to choose unsafe options.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11 and SDG 13

Information: Choose one local topic, read a reliable source, and explain what you learned to classmates, family, or your community. Share the source with your explanation so others can check the information. The challenge is about informed participation, not spreading unverified claims.
Source: World's Largest Lesson; The Global Goals

Information: Identify a public or community space and think of one improvement that could make it cleaner, more accessible, safer, or more welcoming. Discuss the idea with responsible adults or relevant organizations; do not enter restricted areas or undertake work without permission.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11; IMPLAN Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: Community initiatives may explore environmental education, public-space care, waste reduction, water awareness, or civic participation. Before listing an existing initiative, verify its organizer, location, date, contact details, and status. This database contains ideas, not a verified directory of current events.
Source: World's Largest Lesson resources; municipal and IMPLAN planning references

Information: Long-term improvements require contributions from residents, schools, communities, organizations, businesses, and government. Personal actions can complement public policies, infrastructure, investment, maintenance, and accountability. The site should not imply that individuals alone are responsible for solving structural problems.
Source: UN Global Compact — SDGs; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: Invite users to choose a realistic commitment: learn about a local issue, reduce waste, care for a shared space, conserve water, or share verified information. The commitment should be specific and voluntary. It is a reflection activity, not a measure of environmental impact.
Source: Project activity based on The Global Goals and World’s Largest Lesson

Information: IRAPUATO, REIMAGINED is an educational student project about local sustainability, community challenges, and possible futures. It is designed to make local information accessible through interactive storytelling and encourage thoughtful participation. It is not affiliated with or operated by the municipal government.
Source: Project editorial statement

Information: This section introduces the student team, explains why Irapuato was chosen as the focus, and presents the team's motivation for creating the website. Add the team's own names, roles, and video after they are confirmed. This database includes a complete placeholder paragraph so no cell is left blank.
Source: Project editorial statement

Information: The 2050 scenarios are illustrative educational narratives, not scientific forecasts, official predictions, or municipal commitments. Qualitative indicators and interface scores, if used, are design elements and not measured statistics. Local facts must include their source, publication year, and scope.
Source: Project editorial disclaimer; IMPLAN Irapuato

Information: Local statistics in this database are reported in cited municipal documents and retain their original dates and scope. They should not be presented as current measurements unless verified against a newer source. Scenario descriptions are hypothetical. When information is not available, the website should state the limitation rather than invent a value.
Source: Project editorial disclaimer; Government of Irapuato; IMPLAN

Information: Each content card should include a source name and a clickable link to the original document or page. The text is paraphrased for educational use. When adding images, maps, graphics, or datasets, verify their licensing and attribution requirements separately. Do not imply a source supports claims that it does not contain.
Source: Project editorial policy; cited official sources
